scope: Bounded source pass, no exhaustive reading, no cultural/rumor premise admitted as physics

sources.title: Experiments, Portsmouth Add. MS.3973
sources.author: Isaac Newton
sources.version_date: Manuscript entries 10–17 December 1678; scholarly electronic edition 2006
sources.reading_depth: Selected dated entries and manuscript metadata read in normalized scholarly transcription. Entire manuscript and facsimile not read.
sources.provenance: Primary historical laboratory record, mediated by Indiana University scholarly transcription; repository Cambridge University Library.
sources.claim: The selected entries record input and residue weights, observed appearances, and mixtures that did not combine as intended.
sources.relevance: Quantitative operation/error logs and retention of negative outcomes; no alchemical substance or hidden agency is introduced into AQ.
sources.unresolved_verification: Original manuscript images and wider experiment sequence not checked in this pass.

sources.title: Of Natures obvious laws & processes in vegetation, Dibner MS.1031 B
sources.author: Isaac Newton
sources.section: f.1r opening propositions 1–12; f.1v dissimilitudes; rendered lines 350–413
sources.reading_depth: Selected English propositions and dissimilarities read; later passages were search extracts only. Latin treatise and facsimile not read.
sources.provenance: Primary historical theoretical/chymical notes via Indiana University scholarly transcription; manuscript held by Smithsonian Institution Libraries.
sources.claim: The text proposes vegetation and a latent spirit as a common agency, while recording dissimilarities between the compared processes.
sources.relevance: Motivates an explicit analogy-failure control and a demand for operationally identifiable latent variables; no modern physical truth follows from the historical assertion.
sources.unresolved_verification: Dating and complete textual development not investigated; no modern validation of the proposed agency claimed.

sources.title: Observations upon the Prophecies of Daniel, Part I, Chapter II: Of the Prophetic Language
sources.author: Isaac Newton
sources.section: Chapter II opening paragraphs, printed pages 16–19; rendered lines 81–87
sources.reading_depth: Chapter metadata and selected opening interpretive mappings read. Remaining book not read.
sources.provenance: Primary historical theological text via Oxford Newton Project scholarly normalized transcription.
sources.claim: Newton explicitly interprets natural images through a dictionary of political meanings.
sources.relevance: Methodological analogy: expose physical/dimensionless/model dictionaries. The theological interpretation supplies no gauge-theory premise.
sources.unresolved_verification: No physical claim or correspondence between prophecy and measured data was assessed.

sources.title: US645576A, System of transmission of electrical energy
sources.author: Nikola Tesla
sources.section: Description of transmitting/receiving apparatus and rarefied-air demonstration; claims 1–6; rendered lines 164–238, especially 207–218 and 228–238
sources.reading_depth: Selected specification and claims read through patent OCR. Drawings and original PDF scan were not independently inspected in this pass.
sources.provenance: Primary patent specification hosted in Google Patents; its performance statements remain inventor claims.
sources.claim: The described proposal names a generator, transmitting and receiving coils, medium, synchronization and leakage/altitude considerations.
sources.relevance: Whole-mechanism accounting motivates keeping complete factors, endpoint actions and the output state. A granted patent does not certify global energy-transfer performance.
sources.unresolved_verification: OCR ambiguities and historical performance claims not independently experimentally verified.

sources.title: Letter to E. T. Sturdy, 13 February 1896
sources.author: Swami Vivekananda
sources.section: Date/addressee and paragraphs reporting Tesla, Prana/Akasha/Kalpas and an anticipated demonstration; rendered lines 6–17
sources.reading_depth: Letter metadata and Tesla-related paragraphs read. No autograph or missing Tesla calculation inspected.
sources.provenance: Primary contemporary correspondent report through a Complete Works transcription; it is not Tesla-authored mathematical work.
sources.claim: Vivekananda reports Tesla interest in Vedantic ideas and an expectation of a future mathematical demonstration.
sources.relevance: Distinguishes cultural exchange and proposed calculation from an existing theorem. No energy or matter identity is imported.
sources.unresolved_verification: No completed demonstration is present in the inspected passage; later fulfillment not established.

sources.title: Local stability of ground states in locally gapped and weakly interacting quantum spin systems
sources.author: Joscha Henheik, Stefan Teufel, Tom Wessel
sources.version_date: arXiv v3, 2022-03-03; Letters in Mathematical Physics 112, 9 (2022)
sources.section: Section 2 setup, Definitions 1–2, Theorem 3, discussion immediately following Theorem 3, Definition 4/Corollary 5 opening; rendered lines 58–112
sources.reading_depth: Selected theorem statements, assumptions and boundary discussion read; complete proof and numerical constant extraction not performed.
sources.provenance: Primary mathematical research paper by theorem authors.
sources.claim: For sufficiently small finite-range interactions around gapped on-site terms, Theorem 3 bounds local changes caused by a distant perturbation with existential constants.
sources.relevance: AR boundary comparison route. Supports possibly infinite-dimensional factors, but AQ needs a verified threshold and constants in its own dictionary before numerical use.
sources.unresolved_verification: No numeric values of c,c1,c2 certified here; AQ numerical-cap applicability not established.

sources.title: Truncation uncertainties for accurate quantum simulations of lattice gauge theories
sources.author: Anthony N. Ciavarella, Siddharth Hariprakash, Jad C. Halimeh, Christian W. Bauer
sources.version_date: arXiv:2508.00061v2; initial submission 2025-07-31, v2 date not separately checked
sources.section: Section 2.1, equations 4–14; Section 4 discussion; rendered lines 63–94 and 401–406
sources.reading_depth: Selected eigenstate truncation derivation, stated assumptions, and discussion/application limitations read. All appendices, numerical code and error estimates not independently reproduced.
sources.provenance: Primary contemporary research preprint/paper by method authors; version-specific reading.
sources.claim: Electric-basis leakage is estimated using perturbative structure and fragmentation, with factorial suppression of leading contributions and numerical checks.
sources.relevance: Candidate technique for a prospective AQ representation-tail study; cannot replace an independently established remainder for three-dimensional SU(2) complete factors and the chosen state.
sources.unresolved_verification: Inspected applications are Abelian; AQ-specific non-Abelian extension, complete remainder and state replacement remain unverified.

government_records: No government-program source was inspected in this lens pass. A patent is a government-granted record, not government performance validation.
